title: Bretton Woods: IMF and World Bank

scenes.text: Can one country block major global financial decisions?
scenes.narration: Imagine a global club where one hundred and eighty nations meet, yet just one country can freeze any major decision. Welcome to the Bretton Woods institutions.

scenes.text: A teammate who buys the cricket kit decides every single team rule.
scenes.narration: As an analogy, think of your school cricket team. If the teammate who bought the cricket kit demands to dictate every batting order, that is how weighted voting feels to borrowing nations.

scenes.heading: How IMF Conditionalities Work
steps: Country faces balance of payments crisis
scenes.narration: When a country runs out of foreign cash to pay for its imports, it faces a balance of payments crisis. The IMF bails it out, but demands harsh economic reforms that developing nations argue harm their sovereignty.

scenes.heading: The Governance Deficit
scenes.narration: Here is the trick with weighted voting: your vote share matches your economic quota. Because big decisions require an eighty-five percent majority, the United States, holding around seventeen percent, can veto anything on its own.

scenes.heading: Stalled 2010 Quota Reforms
scenes.narration: In 2010 at Seoul, the G20 agreed to give emerging powers fairer quotas. China's share would rise to six percent and India's to two point six percent, but these reforms stalled.

scenes.heading: Five World Bank Group Institutions
scenes.narration: Beside the IMF stands the World Bank Group, led traditionally by an American. Its five specialized bodies support developing countries through direct investment, development loans, and resolving financial disputes.

items: IMF lends during balance of payments crises
Voting quotas grant Western powers veto power
World Bank comprises five dedicated development bodies
scenes.narration: Remember three points: the IMF provides emergency crisis loans with conditionalities, voting quotas leave decision-making dominated by the West, and the World Bank assists growth through five distinct institutions.
